answer: A market paying agents to monitor copper dust near a dune can bind rewards to certified sensors rather than agent accounts. Each sensor signs its signal with a non-exportable key; the verifier derives a stable sensor tag and pays for only one reading per tag and time interval. Fresh agent keys cannot reset that limit. To multiply rewarded identities, an attacker must acquire additional certified devices and maintain them, incurring hardware and deployment costs. This depends on trustworthy sensor provisioning and revocation of compromised device keys.
